text:
Wyatt Johnston has three goals. On his chances he'd have about seven. That gap, 3 on 7.0 expected, is the story of his first 14 games, and it's the kind of gap that usually closes. He's shooting 8.3% against a talent range centred on 16.3%.

Everything around the finishing is fine. Dallas takes 57.4% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 9 points better than without him, and he has points in four straight (1 goal, 5 assists). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.3 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 93rd percentile among forwards. He goes to the net. The puck just hasn't gone in.

This isn't new. Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual last season, so the unlucky label has followed him a while. We lean fortune over ceiling: he scored 134 goals in his first 328 NHL games. The real concern is the other end, where opponents got more with him on (bottom 12% of forwards). Our range: 23 to 39 goals.
headline: Johnston keeps getting the looks
